author: TEDx Talks
description:
Paralympic medalist Isaac Jean-Paul opened his TEDxBeverlyGrove 2026 talk with the doctor who diagnosed him legally blind at two, then told his parents not to hold him back because of what they thought he could not do. What followed was not an inspiration story. It was a case against what he calls the kindness ceiling, when help quietly lowers the standard. Drawing on the coaches who raised his ceiling and the athletes he later coached, Jean-Paul closes with the line that gives the talk its title: we don't handicap people, we handicap environments. Isaac Jean-Paul is a two-time Paralympic medalist (bronze, Tokyo 2020; silver, Paris 2024), world-record holder in high jump, and World Champion (2017 World Para Athletics Championships). He is an NCAA Division II national champion, All-American, and is currently
training to become the first Paralympian to win Olympic gold at the LA 2028 Olympic Games.

At TEDxBeverlyGrove
Isaac Jean-Paul will share “We Don’t Handicap People. We Handicap En
title: We Don't Handicap People. We Handicap Environments. | Isaac Jean-Paul | TEDxBeverly Grove

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the way we give is getting in the way of the change we want to create?

Andrew Dayton challenges the idea that wealth should be treated as a proxy for wisdom in philanthropy. Instead, he argues for giving guided by evidence, measurable outcomes, and the wisdom of the communities closest to the problems.

By focusing less on donor preferences and more on what actually works, philanthropy can help prove solutions that lead to broader, lasting change.

Sometimes, the most powerful thing a donor can do is step out of the way.
 Andrew Dayton is the founder and CEO of the Constellation Fund, a Minnesota-based foundation dedicated to effective poverty alleviation. Constellation deploys rigorous data and analytics to identify, fund, and empower the people and organizations making the greatest measurable impact on poverty in the Twin Cities. Through its research arm, CoLab, Constellation also catalyzes and funds longitudinal research on what actually drives economic mobility.

Before f
title: The Generosity Paradox | Andrew Dayton | TEDxFargo

author: TEDx Talks
description: In a world grappling with climate extremes, soil depletion, and food security demands, we can no longer rely solely on traditional breeding. Scott Jackson, founder of the Institute for Crop Design at the University of Georgia, shares how AI-powered modeling, precision genome engineering, and next-generation plant breeding are ushering in a new era of intentional crop design. Drawing from decades of experience—from sequencing legume genomes to leading R&D teams in the seed industry and now building disruptive solutions at UGA—he demonstrates real-world examples. This talk explores the design-build-test-learn cycle that accelerates innovation, turning data, biology, and breeding into tools for resilient, high-value crops. Discover how we move from selecting nature’s offerings to designing the abundant, sustainable food systems of tomorrow. Scott Jackson is a plant geneticist, agricultural innovator, and Georgia Research Alliance Eminent Scholar in Synthetic Biology at the University of
title: Designing Tomorrow's Harvest: AI and a New Era of Crop Engineering | Scott Jackson | TEDxFargo

author: TEDx Talks
description:
As our country celebrates its 250th birthday, too many of us feel as if the American Dream is dying. Yet the American Dream is not just about financial success – it’s about creating a good society where the opportunity to achieve is held in common.

In this talk, Tony Pipa, host of the Reimagine Rural podcast and founder of the Reimagining Rural Policy initiative at the Brookings Institution, describes how rural communities are demonstrating that renewal of the American Dream relies on healthy civic structures, where people use their talents, capabilities, and creativity to keep their hometowns vibrant and vital. In an era of polarization and pessimism, he tells the story of places in rural America undergoing a civic renaissance that offer a path forward for the rest of the country – if we embrace it. Tony Pipa is a senior fellow in the Center for Sustainable Development at the Brookings Institution. Pipa launched and leads the Reimagining Rural Policy initiative and hosts the award-w
title: Why renewing the American Dream runs through rural America | Tony Pipa | TEDxFargo

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We often blame politicians, billionaires, lobbyists, the media, or social media for the problems facing our communities and our country. But what if we're overlooking the most important part of the equation: ourselves?

Political columnist and writer Rob Port takes a provocative look at modern American politics and argues that voters have more responsibility for the government they criticize than they may want to admit.

From the national debt and competing demands for taxes and government services to the influence of social media and the high rate at which incumbents are reelected, Port examines the tension between what Americans say they want from government and the choices they make at the ballot box.

His challenge is uncomfortable but straightforward: democracy doesn't just ask us to choose our leaders. It asks us to take responsibility for the choices we make. Rob Port was a pioneer in political blogging in North Dakota, founding SayAnythingBlog.com in 2003. Before beginning his
title: Blame the voters. | Rob Port | TEDxFargo

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if your calling isn't one perfect destination, but something that changes as you do?

Terry Brandt begins with the remarkable story of Larry Walters, who attached weather balloons to a lawn chair to pursue his dream of flying. What started as a short trip above his neighborhood unexpectedly carried him 16,000 feet into the sky—and into a dramatic rescue. But for Terry, Walters' story is about more than a homemade flying machine. It's about being willing to pursue a dream while still being “wonderfully scared.”

Drawing from Lutheran theology and his own journey from teacher to pastor, camp director, bishop, and foundation executive, Terry offers a different way to think about calling. Rather than a single point we can either find or miss, calling exists at the intersection of our gifts, our passions, and the needs of the world—and those things are always changing.

Terry explores how listening both inwardly and to the people who know us best can help reveal where we're being call
title: Are you flying high? | Terry Brandt | TEDxFargo

author: TEDx Talks
description: We are often told to let anger go, stay calm and be the bigger person. Célia Kamdom asks a different question: what if rage can be transformed instead of swallowed? She explores the energy behind revenge and the choice to redirect it away from destruction and toward creation. The result is not a celebration of anger, but a reframing of what we can do with it. Sometimes the most powerful response to what hurt us is to build something real. A life, a project or a future that becomes its own answer. Célia Kamdom is a technology professional, entrepreneur and founder of Oriaku Studio, a design brand connecting African craftsmanship with Scandinavian minimalism. Her professional background spans technology, change management and entrepreneurship, while her creative work is rooted in questions of heritage, recognition and making something new from competing worlds. In her TEDx talk, Célia turns to another powerful source of creative energy: rage. Rather than romanticizing anger or treating
title: The Power of Rage | Célia Kamdom | TEDxFredrikstad

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the small decisions you make every day are quietly shaping the person you become? 

This emotional and personal talk explores how fear of judgment can turn into a cycle of avoidance and what happens when we finally choose to move forward, even while we are still afraid.

In this personal and thought provoking talk, Raissa Pahlevi reflects on a moment when she wanted to step onto the stage but chose to stay backstage, revealing how fear of judgment can shape not only our decisions, but also the way we see ourselves.

Blending her personal experience with insights from psychology, Raissa explores the spotlight effect, the brain’s response to fear, and the reinforcement loop that can make avoidance feel like a natural choice. 

She invites us to look closer at the small decisions we make every day and asks whether we are truly choosing what we want or simply choosing what feels safe

 Raissa Pahlevi is a 15 year old student at Avicenna Cinere Junior High School. She loves explori
title: The Decision: Breaking the Cycle of Avoidance | Raissa Pahlevi | TEDxAvicenna Cinere School

description: Losing on the outside is winning on the inside. Nele is a 9th Grade Student at Franconian International School. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Losing on the outside is winning on the inside. | Nele Zeitler | TEDxYouth@TFIS

author: TEDx Talks
description: After travelling to every country in the world twice, Gunnar Garfors has learned a surprising amount about how not to travel. He shares the mistakes, misunderstandings and small scandals that taught him why copying the same social-media itineraries can flatten the very thing we travel to experience. With humor and hard-earned perspective, he argues for more independent travel: talk to people, leave space for surprise, and stop outsourcing your holiday to someone else's feed. Meaningful travel often begins when we stop following the herd. Gunnar Garfors is a Norwegian author, world-record traveller and founder of The Garfors Globe. He has travelled to every country in the world twice and spent years on the road collecting both extraordinary experiences and spectacular mistakes. His books and talks focus less on ticking places off a list than on how we meet people and cultures once we arrive. Having repeatedly misunderstood customs, taken the wrong route and learned the hard way, Gunnar
title: How not to travel | Gunnar Garfors | TEDxFredrikstad

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the story of your life didn’t begin with you?

A Common Destiny explores the connections between our personal stories and the stories that came before us. Through CHAPI MWANGO, the talk invites us to look at how shared experiences, inherited narratives, and human connection shape who we are and where we are going.

Presented as part of TEDxArada’s theme, “The Seriousness of Play,” the talk encourages us to see play not simply as entertainment, but as a way of exploring identity, connection, and the possibilities of a shared future. Chapi Mwango is a Policy Professional and storyteller whose work explores the intersection of identity, leadership, and human connection across África. Born between Zambian and Ethiopian heritage and raised in Addis Ababa, his journey across cultures and continents has shaped a deeply reflective perspective on belonging, governance, and shared destiny. Through his work within development and public speaking, Chapi is passionate about building bridge
title: A common Destiny  | Chapi Mwango | TEDxArada Play

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Un repaso por la vida de mi hijo mayor, Alan , y como su autismo fue y es sinónimo de enseñanza y superación para él mismo  y para mí. El valorar las pequeñas cosas como importantes y lo que parece una tragedia solo un mal momento.
Sin lenguaje, te podes comunicar. Sin avances madurativos, puedes madurar. O sea crecer y hacerlo juntos  Entrenador de handball de más de 40 años, padre y esposo apasionado y amante perruno hasta la médula. Y que fue aprendiendo, de mas grande, a ser mejor padre. Una “Carrera” sin fin. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Alan y papa. Creciendo en azul | Fernando Capurro | TEDxEsquel

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In a world where students are expected to excel at everything, success often comes at an unseen cost. In this thought-provoking talk, Vidushi Katiyar explores the pressure of being a high-achieving multi-hyphenate and the silent burnout that follows. Reflecting on a defining incident from an eighth-grade play, she examines the fear of failure, the burden of constant expectations, and why psychological safety is essential for young people to thrive. Through candid storytelling, Vidushi reminds us that our worth is not measured by flawless performance, but by the courage to embrace imperfection and keep growing. Vidushi Katiyar is a 17-year-old multi-hyphenate driven by an insatiable curiosity for the world around her. Her journey reflects a dynamic blend of creative arts such as dance, painting, music, and drama, alongside the high-energy discipline of sports and karate.
Being a “jack of all trades” has not always been easy for her, as she has navigated significant mental and social ch
title: Spoiler Alert! | Vidushi Katiyar | TEDxSAJS Vasundhara Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: With infinite content right in our pockets, we should be the ultimate masters of our own choices, interests, and beliefs. But we aren't. That's because our everyday decisions are being hijacked by the algorithms of the 21'st century, designed to keep us watching irrelevant documentaries at 3:30 AM. In this witty and eye-opening talk, Rishi Joshi reveals how we unwittingly surrendered our autonomy to the algorithm. Exploring everything from 'Subway Surfers' attention spans to the dangerous erosion of human civilization and humanity itself, he breaks down the doom-scroll, the loss of cognitive ability and individualism, and how to reclaim our most essential human trait: the freedom to choose for ourselves. Rishi Joshi is a 16-year-old who takes a keen interest in conversations that challenge beliefs, bring people together, and create awareness or drive change. He actively participates in Model United Nations conferences, engages in interschool debates, and writes articles to express his
title: How We Are Surrendering our Autonomy to Algorithms | Rishi Joshi | TEDxSAJS Vasundhara Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: The two eyes hold discipline and creativity - one, the order; the other, the madness. But we see only one image, always. Do they live as separate ideas - one, the rigour; the other, the exploration? Or are they, the same - the foundation that strengthens the flight? Divya Goswami is a Kathak dancer known for her graceful performances and strong command over this classical Indian dance form. Through her dedication and training, she brings rhythm, expression, and storytelling together, showcasing the rich cultural heritage of Kathak. Her work reflects discipline, artistry, and a deep passion for dance, connecting traditional techniques with engaging stage presence. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Discipline- The Rhythm of Creativity | Divya Goswami | TEDxSAJS Vasundhara Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Sport teaches you much more than how to win. Bhawna Jaiswal shares how discipline, independence and resilience shaped her journey and why we don’t always have to choose just one passion or one identity to build a meaningful life. Bhawna Jaiswal believes that strength is built as much through words as through action. An athlete, poet, and creator from Bhopal, she shares stories that remind us that our greatest transformations often begin after the first victory. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Ek Pehchan Kaafi Nahi | Bhawna Jaiswal | TEDxShahpura Lake

author: TEDx Talks
description: How young is too young to start building the future? Through his experiments with electronics, robotics and AI, eight-year-old Lakshveer Rao challenges the assumption that children must wait to grow up before they can explore, create and solve problems. An 8-year-old young innovator exploring AI, robotics, electronics and hardware through hands-on building and experimentation. His projects span intelligent devices, accessibility solutions, and AI systems designed to work even without internet access. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Too Young To Try | Lakshveer Rao | TEDxShahpura Lake

description: What if sustainability begins not with what we recycle, but with what we refuse? Prof. Himanshu Rai explores the difference between needs and desires and introduces a powerful fourth R—Refuse—as a way to rethink our choices and our relationship with consumption. An acclaimed academic leader, author, and storyteller. Through his insights on leadership, ethics, and purpose, he inspires individuals to rethink the choices that shape their lives and careers. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Journey of Swadharma | Dr. Himanshu Rai | TEDxShahpura Lake

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The Fifth Dimension,” explores the idea that beyond the physical dimensions of space and time lies another dimension that shapes our lives: perspective. Through my experiences working with students and building communities, I will explore how two people can live in the same world yet see completely different possibilities, not because of differences in talent but because of differences in exposure and the way they see themselves and their future. The talk will challenge the invisible and borrowed limitations we carry and explore how expanding our perspective can transform walls into doors and limitations into possibilities. "Shashank Misra is a community builder and growth leader on a mission to empower young people to become the leaders of tomorrow. He is building Student Tribe, one of India's largest student communities, creating platforms that connect students with opportunities, ideas, industry, and each other.

His work goes beyond networking and engagement it's about building an
title: The Fifth Dimension: Where Possibility Begins | Shashank Misra | TEDxKPRIT

author: TEDx Talks
description: We’re often told to choose one path, specialize, and stay consistent with it. But what if being curious about many things is actually a strength? My journey across content creation, acting, art and technology has taught me that growth doesn’t always happen on the timeline we expect. It took me three years to cross 100k through content creation, and I don’t shy away from how long it took. I believe everyone has a different timeline, and slow progress doesn’t mean you’re failing. This talk is about embracing different interests, pushing yourself beyond perceived limits, staying consistent when results are slow, and continuing to show up even when nobody else sees the potential yet. Vikshitha V is a student, content creator, actor and multidisciplinary creative with a strong belief in exploring beyond a single path. Her work spans content creation, acting, art and technology, driven by my curiosity to learn, create and constantly challenge herself. She always believed she can do more, ev
title: The Power of Not Choosing Just One Path | Vikshitha V | TEDxKPRIT

author: TEDx Talks
description:
"Designing Minds That Will Design Tomorrow” explores how education must move beyond conventional measures such as marks, grades, and memory to nurture curiosity, creativity, critical thinking, purpose and meaningful impact. Drawing from the teaching profession, the talk connects the Fifth Dimension, Knowledge, Technology, Leadership, Purpose, and Impact to a new vision of education where teachers do not merely transfer knowledge but design minds capable of solving tomorrow’s challenges and shaping a better future. Dr. S. Sreenath Kashyap is an academic leader, researcher, and Principal at KPRIT College of Engineering , Hyderabad.
 He holds a Post Doctoral Degree from the University of South Florida, USA and MBA from IIM Kashipur, also a PhD in Electronics and Communication Engineering. His research spans AI, VLSI, Microwave Engineering, Antennas, and sensor technologies, with numerous publications, patents, and authored books. As a PhD supervisor, speaker, and educator, he champions i
title: Designing Minds That Will Design Tomorrow | Sreenath kashyap S | TEDxKPRIT

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In her TEDx Talk, Malika Bobokhujayeva explores the fascinating connection between language and identity. She dives into why people often feel more confident, emtional, reserved, or expressive depending on the language they speak - and how multilingualism can quitely shape the way we think, feel, and connect with others.
Through this talk, she reveals how language is more than communication; it becomes a lens through which we experience the world and ourselves. Her central message is simple yet powerful: every language we speak unlocks a different side of who we are.  Malika Bobokhujaeva is a multilingual speaker, IELTS instructor, and education advocate passionate about languages, communication, and the psychology of learning. Having achieved an IELTS Band 8.0, she speaks Uzbek, English, Russian, Tajik, and Turkish, with additional knowledge of Arabic and Korean. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Lear
title: Different Language, Different You | Malika Bobokhujayeva | TEDxTKA Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
"You have everything" - a phrase that sounds supportive on the surface, yetoften overlooks something critical. In her TEDx Talk, Laziza Mahkamova explores how emotional struggles are  frequently dismissed simply because someone appears successful, priviliged, or 'fine' from the outside.
She reflects on the hidden pressure to constantly seem grateful, accomplished, and emotionally stable while silently battling feelings of emptiness, anxiety, and isolation.
Through this talk, Laziza challenges the way we define well-being and reminds us that mental and emotional struggles do not disappear just because a person has opportunities, achievements, or support around them. Laziza Makhkamova is 15 years old and a school student with a strong interest in psychology, chess, and the humanities. This is her third TED Talk, where she spoke on the topic “But You Have Everything — And I Still Was Drowning.”

In her talk, Laziza addresses an important and often overlooked issue: the fear or shame of s
title: "You Have Everything"-And I Was Still Drowning | Laziza Makhamova | TEDxTKA Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
AI is changing more than how we access information. It is changing what we are able to do with it.

In this talk, Anchit Nishant explores how AI is beginning to close the distance between intention and action—turning knowledge and information into something that can be translated into real-world capability.

For decades, technological progress has made information faster and more accessible. But the next shift may be about what happens after we have the information: our ability to act on it.

The next revolution, he argues, is not simply about having more information. It is about turning information into capability. Anchit Nishant works at the frontier where AI moves from possibility into practice. 

As a Solutions Architect at OpenAI, with more than a decade across Google and Amazon, he helps organizations design and scale technology systems that are useful, reliable and responsible in the real world.

His work sits at the intersection of generative AI, cloud architecture and human o
title: AI Is Turning Information Into Capability  | Anchit Nishant | TEDxSukhna Lake

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if excellence is not about doing something exceptionally well, but first asking whether you are doing the right thing?

In this thought-provoking talk, Dr Pramod Bhargav explores the relationship between relevance, education and excellence. He challenges us to look beyond simply becoming better at what we do and first understand whether what we are learning and doing is relevant to the world around us.

Because when education is truly relevant, excellence doesn't have to be forced—it follows naturally.

The key, he suggests, is to keep being curious: to question, explore, learn and stay open to what the world needs.

Before asking “How well can I do this?” perhaps we should ask, “Is this the right thing to do?” An accomplished academician with 20 years of experience a researcher with almost 50 publications and an author with 7 books. He holds a Ph.D., M.Phil., M.Com., and UGC-NET qualification, specializing in Accounting, Finance, Cost Management, and Financial Analysis. ,he guid
title: Relevance Before Excellence: Are You Doing the Right Thing? | Dr. Pramod Bhargava | TEDxSukhna Lake

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this talk, Milind Kelkar points out that many people have the right credentials and experience yet still find themselves shuffling in and out of entry-level positions and jobs they don’t like. They see the alternative, entrepreneurship, as a road blocked by the obstacle of financial capital. He explores the idea that although financial capital speaks the loudest in entrepreneurship, it is not necessarily the most important. He describes three other types of capital, namely social capital, creative capital and cultural capital and how these can play a role in entrepreneurship no matter your financial capital.
 An AI scientist, product builder, and systems thinker who has spent more than 25 years helping organisations make better decisions in complex environments.
His career has spanned analytics, machine learning, marketing science, research, and AI-powered platforms across organisations including Genpact, WNS, HSBC, and Kantar. Today, he leads Unpickle, where he focuses on designin
title: You will never walk alone if you build the right capital | Milind Kelkar | TEDxRVCE

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the difficult things life puts in our way are also teaching us how to navigate what comes next?

In this deeply personal talk, Lalit Agnihotri traces his journey from growing up in a family with limited means to building a career across organisations such as Eureka Forbes and KFC India. At the centre of his story is an unlikely teacher: a small electrical repair shop where, as a young boy, he learned a simple lesson—when something stops working, don't complain. Open it, understand it, find the fault and repair it.

Because sometimes, the thing that is broken isn't the end of the story. It may simply be waiting for someone to open it and look inside. Lalit Agnihotri is a Business Transformation Strategist, Entrepreneur, Leadership Mentor & Founder of Temple of Growth (TOG). Known as the “One-Man Army,” he has spent over 3 decades helping businesses grow through strategy, execution and continuous improvement. He began his career as an assistant electrician and rose through perse
title: What Repair Shop Taught Me: How to Turn Setbacks into Strength | Lalit Agnihotri | TEDxSukhna Lake

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if your happy ending was actually your beginning?

Raised on Bollywood's idea that marriage is the destination, physiotherapist and founder of Peak Performance found that her real story started after the credits rolled.

From being the only woman physio on a FIFA & AIFF campus, to being thrown out of her own startup in Bangalore while 3-months pregnant, to opening her clinic on 1st May 2016 with a 2-month-old baby and a golden retriever as her first staff.

Just when life felt stable, 6 weeks postpartum in 2026, a sudden heart attack landed her in the ICU for 3 days, unable to feed her newborn.

This is not a story about what happened to her. It's about the one choice we all have: *Stop Spiraling. Start Showing Up.
 Dr. Dipali Pandey is a leading Sports Physiotherapist and the visionary founder of Peak Performance, a premier wellness ecosystem dedicated to ethical, evidence-based rehabilitation. With a background in elite sports medicine, Dr. Pandey has served as the physiotherap
title: Go Twist The Plot | Stop Spiralling, Start Showing Up | | Dr. Dipali Pandey | TEDxMLAC Women

author: TEDx Talks
description: We’re often told what a successful life should look like. Priyanka Rudrappa chose to question that script. From choosing Home Science when everyone expected her to pursue biotechnology, to returning from the UK during the 2008 recession, her journey took several unexpected turns. Each one eventually led her closer to building something of her own—a design studio centred on customisation and detail. But this isn’t just a story about fashion or entrepreneurship. It’s about finding the confidence to make your own choices, becoming financially and emotionally independent, and refusing to let other people decide what your life should look like. Sometimes, a plot twist is exactly what sets you free. Priyanka Rudrappa is the Founder and CEO of Café Amudham, a fast-growing South Indian café brand built on a deep love for authentic, comforting food. Founded in 2022, Café Amudham reflects her belief that traditional recipes can be thoughtfully brought into modern spaces without losing their sou
title: Who Gets to Write Your Life? | Priyanka Rudrappa | TEDxMLAC Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Sonika spoke about how everyday technology quietly collects information about our sleep, health, habits, and choices. She highlighted how, when combined at scale, personal data can reveal patterns and make people easier to understand, predict, or influence.

Her talk encouraged people to become more aware of their digital footprint and make thoughtful choices about what personal information they share. Sonika Pilli is a healthtech entrepreneur passionate about making healthcare more accessible, relevant, and meaningful for the next generation.

With a strong interest in technology and innovation, she is working to shape better healthcare experiences for Gen Z. Beyond entrepreneurship, Sonika is also a trained classical dancer, balancing creativity with purpose. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
